questions.q: What does a dataset actually represent?
options: The connection information needed to reach a data store
A named view pointing to specific data — a table, file, or folder — inside a linked service
A scheduled time for a pipeline to run
A visual chart built from pipeline monitoring data
questions.explain: A dataset points to specific data reachable through a linked service. The linked service is the connection; the dataset is what inside that connection you actually mean.

questions.q: Where do you go in Data Factory Studio to create a new dataset?
options: The Monitor hub
The Home page's Configure SSIS tile
Datasets can only be created via PowerShell, not the Studio UI
The Author hub, select the + icon, then Dataset
questions.explain: Author hub → + icon → Dataset opens the same connector gallery used for linked services, then walks through format and connection selection.

questions.q: What does a dataset's "format" setting actually specify?
options: The color scheme used to display the dataset in Monitor
Whether the dataset is public or private
Which Azure region the dataset's data lives in
How the underlying data is structured — DelimitedText, JSON, Parquet, Binary, and so on
questions.explain: Format describes the physical shape of the data itself — a CSV needs DelimitedText, a columnar file needs Parquet, and so on.

options: Converts the dataset to a different file format automatically
Publishes the dataset to the Power BI service
Reads the actual column names and types directly from the live source
Deletes the dataset's existing schema permanently
questions.explain: Import Schema reads the real shape of the data straight from the source — the right default almost every time, versus basing it on a local file when no live source is available yet.

questions.q: Can a single linked service support more than one dataset?
options: Only in Fabric Data Factory, never in Azure Data Factory
Yes — one linked service can back many datasets, each pointing at a different location within it
Only if both datasets use the exact same file format
No — each dataset requires its own separate linked service
questions.explain: Since a linked service only defines the connection, many datasets can reuse the same one, each pointing at a different container, folder, file, or table.
